title: A run-outcome ledger per spec version

story.i_want_to: every dispatch to end in one outcome row keyed by its spec {id, version}, with what later happened to its work
story.so_that: each agent's track record is a query, and the improvement loop (US-48.13) learns from what humans and gates did with the output rather than from the agent's own report

rationale: Mark, 2026-11-07: "we need some kind of a feedback loop built-in, so these agents would self-improve as they work." A loop can only improve on a signal it records. The KB's account of the production-to-eval cycle (4efb55d0, a349c48f) starts from traces turned into evals; today a run's fate is scattered over the ledger, stage history and GitHub.

acceptance_criteria.description: Table agent_run_outcomes (tenant_id, RLS): one row per dispatch, unique on dispatch_id, carrying spec_id, spec_version, prompt template {id, version}, story_id, project_id, started_at, ended_at, elapsed_s, turns, end_reason, and cost where the runner reported it.

Downstream signals are appended to the row as they happen, each from the system event that proves it, never from session text: for :judge, whether a human overrode the verdict (resolve_escalation to a different route, or re-triage); for :build, merge gate decision, review finding count by severity, CI result, merged or not, and whether it was re-queued after a budget kill; for :draft, released / edited / discarded.
Writes are idempotent: a redelivered session-end or a repeated gate event leaves the row unchanged (keyed on dispatch_id plus signal name).

Agents.Outcomes.summary(tenant_id, spec_id, opts) returns per-version counts and rates (success, human override, budget exhausted, median elapsed and turns) over a window; MCP tool agent_outcomes calls it, in the same change.
Tenant isolation: one tenant's outcomes never appear in another's summary.

test_cases.name: an implement run's row fills in through merge
steps: dispatch, end the session, record the gate allow, the review findings and the merge
expected_results: one row with every signal, each from its event

test_cases.name: a human override of a triage verdict is recorded
expected_results: human_override true on the triage row

technical_notes: The row is written by control-side effects already on each path (session_ended, merge_precondition, resolve_escalation); no new runner message.
